title: Dave Bailey and the Liberty Bell band
summary: Morris recalls Dave Bailey and the Liberty Bell band members, Blind Freddy and Wesley Dime.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Who were the great clarinetists? Favorites and rivals

blocks.x: We were talking about Dave Bailey
Yeah Yeah Yeah Dave Bailey I was a little bit of boy when Dave was playing He don't look it though do he? No Yeah he gone down now plenty though He can't take all that walking right now
Well now you said something about the Liberty Bell?
Yeah that was the band name

Dave Bailey, Duck Ernest, Forstaff, Cornette player was a dude Foster's brother Foster's brother Foster's brother yeah Then after Foster, he got into the band too Yeah so that's why they used to go and They had a nice little band Then after they put Dude out And they took Wesley Dime He the one that got killed in Baton-Lewis He was a nice little corner of that band And then Blind Freddy too Used to play in there Don't care why you tell him me that he could meet there And he had no eyes at all but he could play And he'd be well dressed up and everything But Blind Freddy'd be there Don't know how he'd get there, he'd get there
But could he uh... How did he compare with Blind Freddy with the best clarinet players for head?
Well I don't know but Blind Freddy was good Must have just had a gift I guess the Lord just give him that gift to make a living Yeah and he had one too
Sounds like a good band, did you ever work with him? Yeah I used to play with him
But I played with Wesley Dime in the band See he got killed in Baton-Lewis Yeah He was a little bit of foul but he could play nice corners
